source.title: No-Go Theorem for Gaussian Quantum Repeaters from Fractional Extendibility

theorem_scope.allowed_operations: Gaussian operations, homodyne measurements and classical communication; theorem also treats arbitrary Gaussian LOCC for two-way capacities
theorem_scope.conclusion: Gaussian repeaters do not increase the specified quantum/private capacities beyond direct transmission under the stated assumptions

project_relevance: Conditional architecture guardrail only; no evidence currently shows that UQPU provider integration depends on this repeater family.
non_claims: does not rule out all quantum repeaters or all quantum networks
does not establish a UQPU hardware, memory, compute or cost advantage
does not apply automatically to non-Gaussian operations or different channel/resource assumptions
does not establish a new physical law
next_gate: For any proposed repeater path, freeze channel model, operation set, resource assumptions, target capacity/fidelity, direct-transmission baseline and full preparation/memory/measurement/communication/cost boundary before simulation.
